rows.author: D023
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING AND ESTABLISHING THE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES SYSTEM (EMSS) IN THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS NATURE, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIE S, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed bill seeks to institute an Emergency Medical Services System (EMSS) in the Philippines. This system will serve as a chain of coordinated services that will provide QUALITY EMERGENCY CARE to those who are ill or injured. Under the EMSS,a call for help is processed quickly and efficiently. The basic life saving techniques and advanced life support measures are delivered early to the patient and properly and immediately transported to the appropriate health facility.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.author: D023
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ANY PERSON, ORGANIZATION OR  COMPANY WHICH POLLUTE CREEKS, LAKES AND RIVERS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to penalize any person, group, organization or corporation polluting creeks or rivers.  Any person who unlawfully discharges oil, noxious, or toxic gaseous and liquid substances and other harmful substances shall be liable, for the first offense, to a fine of not less than five thousand pesos (P5,000.00) but not more than ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) for the second offense to a fine of not less than ten (10) thousand pesos but not more than fifteen (15) thousand pesos; and, for the third offense, to a fine of not less than fifteen (15) thousand pesos but more than twenty (20) thousand pesos.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05398

rows.title_full: AN ACT OFFICIALLY ACKNOWLEDGING THE HEROISM OF BISHOP GREGORIO AGLIPAY
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In celebration of the Centennial of the 1896 Philippine Revolution, it is but proper to officially acknowledge the heroism of Bishop Gregorio Aglipay. There is no more proper and fitting way for the Filipino people and our country to give our tribute to the revolutionary priest who painstakingly fought for our independence. It is because of him that we are reaping the fruits of an independent Philippines.

rows.abstract: Rationale: LABOR-ONLY CONTRACTING is perceived to be a tool which favors the employers since it avoids fixed labor costs, to the detriment of workers. Thus, the prohibition on labor-only contracting will not only afford full protection to workers but would also ensure that the welfare and working conditions of workers are monitored and regulated.

rows.abstract: The proposed measure seeks to amend Articles 135 and 137 of the Labor Code (PD 442, amended) so as to expand the prohibited acts of discrimination against women that it shall be unlawful for any employer to deny any woman the benefits of employmentor other statutory benefits under our laws by reason of her sex, age, ethnic origin or beliefs or relations by affinity or consanguinity.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FRANKING PRIVILEGES TO SANGGUNIANG BARANGAYS
rows.abstract: The franking privilege is hereby granted to Sangguniang barangays. For this purpose the Sangguniang barangays shall be exempt from the payment of postage on any mail matter they send to government agencies and officials, both local and national: Provided, That this exemption shall only be available to assist and expedite the conduct of the official businesses, activities and duties of the Sangguniang barangays, and shall not be utilized for matters which are purely personal or politically partisan.

rows.abstract: There shall be established a National Identification Card System (NICS) for persons residing in the Republic of the Philippines. The National Identification Card (NIC) issued shall serve as a valid proof of identity of the person indicated on the card.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING LOCAL HOUSING BOARDS IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e Local Housing Boards which will be created at the level of local government units. Because of their direct governance of their respective constituencies, the local governments are in the best position to know thepeculiarities of their locality and establish their priorities. Local housing boards, which shall be composed of representatives coming from the public as well as the private sector and civil society, shall be responsible for the formulation of a housing program in their respective areas of jurisdiction.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, RATIONALIZING THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND CORPORATIONS RELATED TO HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to create a DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT to rationalize the shelter and urban development program of the national government. It will streamline the bureaucracy and the process of formulating human settlement programsto meet the demands of our increasing population and decreasing space.  As a full-pledge Department, the shelter program shall likewise be elevated in priority and the attention given by national government to the problem of shelter will become focused and significant.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04517

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT OFFICER IN THE PROVINCIAL, CITY AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: Human value management looks upon people as constituting one of the most important assets of an organization. There us a need to seek a new, more pragmatic and more opportunistic style of human resources management. There is a need to project a new image of human resources as a value-adding function. Human Resources Management is a process by which any organization has to get people, which is recruitment, placement, and job analysis. It includes performance management systems, appraisal systems and reward systems.

rows.abstract: To put more teeth to existing policies and legal provisions on the support and care of children, the State shall hereby punish all parents, guardians, or persons having legal custody of the child and who fail to support and provide for the compulsory education of such.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE COMPUTERIZATION OF GOVERNMENT TRANSACTIONS AND PROCEDURES
rows.abstract: All government transactions shall, to the extent possible, be conducted with the use of computer technology in lieu of manual procedures and systems.  The National Computer Center shall design, install and maintain, with private sector participation, the necessary computer systems in all government offices over a period of one year and upon the implementation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SAFETY NETS THAT WOULD ENABLE THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR TO ADJUST TO AND BE MORE COMPETITIVE IN THE FACE OF THE GENERAL AGREEMENT OF TARIFFS AND TRADE (GATT), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Among the victims of injustice are those in the far-flung barangays who, due to scarcity of lawyers, have to suffer delays in court litigations even for just minor offenses. Some have been detained in jail longer than the penalty they are supposed to serve. The few available lawyers in these places have to seek for several postponements of the hearing of cases they are handling, as they cannot cope with the attendant preparation for the case, documentation and indepth study of the case. The institution of a NATIONAL PARA-LEGAL SYSTEM could minimize such problem.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: "FREEDOM FROM NUCLEAR WEAPONS ACT OF 2001"
rows.abstract: Any provision to the contrary nothwithstandin g, it shall be unlawful for any person to manufacture, possess, store, produce, trade or distribute nuclear weapons within the Philippine territory.  It shall also be unlawful for any war vessel of foreign registry to pass to and from Philippine territorial waters if said vessel stores nuclear weapons in said vessel.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DESIGNATING A SPECIAL EMERGENCY TELEPHONE NUMBER ACCESSIBLE NATIONWIDE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  In an archipelagicall y-oriented country, it is therefore important that an effective communication system be developed to centralize rescue operations not only in the metropolis but also in the far-flung areas of the Philippines especially in times of national disasters and other calamities. This bill, therefore, seeks to create a TOLL-FREE EMERGENCY HOTLINE NUMBER available nationwide.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL PARA-LEGAL SYSTEM IN THE BARANGAY LEVEL
rows.abstract: With the institution of a national para-legal system such problem could be minimized even in the lower courts, such as the Municipal Trial Courts and Municipal Circuit Trial Courts.  A non-lawyer may be allowed to appear before such courts to represent a party litigant but with authority from the Supreme Court.  It is envisioned that the System would function well with the participation of respected persons in the barangay who shall guide and assist the members of the community in their court problems.  The institution of a NATIONAL PARA-LEGAL SYSTEM could minimize such problem.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 70 (d) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 BY REDUCING THE PRESENT REQUIREMENT FOR INITIATING RECALL FROM TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) TO TWENTY PERCENT (20%) OF THE TOTAL REGISTERED VOTERS DURING THE ELECTION OF A CONCERNED OFFICIAL
rows.abstract: With the increasing incidence of local government officials being linked to illegal activities such as murder and illegal gambling, there is a need to amend the provisions for recall of local officials in the Local Government Code. The present requirement of tenty-five percent (25%) of registered voters needed to initiate the recall procedure is unrealistic since it is a requirement that is very difficult to meet.  This requirement actually prevents the people from exercising their lawful remedy of the people to recall an erring local official.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: The Commission shall have the general objective of improving, through research, consultation, and extension, the production of grains in the country.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 450 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, BY INCREASING THE AVERAGE ANNUAL INCOME REQUIREMENT FOR A MUNICIPALITY OR CLUSTER OF BARANGAYS TO BE CONVERTED INTO A COMPONENT CITY
rows.abstract: Section 450 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 450. Requisites for Creation.  (a) A municipality or a cluster of barangays may be converted into a componentcity if it has [an] A LOCALLY GENERATED average annual income, as certified by the Department of Finance, of at least [Twenty Million Pesos (P20,000,000.00 )] ONE HUNDRED MILLION PESOS (P100,000,000.0 0) for the last two (2) consecutive years based on [1991] 2001 constant prices.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THE MECHANISM FOR THE CREATION OF ANTI-ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT DESK IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract: The proposed ANTI-ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT DESK is tasked to: (a) Receive complaints of victims of illegal recruitment (b) Disseminate information to job seekers on acts of illegal recruitment (c) Document and monitor cases of illegal recruitment (d) Submit reports and coordinate with the national offices of Department of Labor and Employment, Philippine Overseas Employment Administration, National Labor Relations Commission, and Department of Justice on cases of illegal recruitment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT FIXING THE SPECIFIC LIMITS OF FORESTLANDS AND NON-FORESTLANDS FOR THE PURPOSE OF PROTECTING, CONSERVING AND ENHANCING THE FOREST RESOURCES OF THE COUNTRY TO ATTAIN ECOLOGICAL BALANCE
rows.abstract: Rationale:  To date, there is no law fixing the total area in the country as forestlands. It is imperative that a specific area for forestlands be established, otherwise, lands previously considered forests will gradually vanish. Unless we set a boundary beyond which lands established as forestlands can no longer be diminished the time will come when we will wake up to find no more forests left in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE INTO THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES
rows.abstract: The conversion of the Department of Agriculture into the DEPARTMENT OF AAGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES would ensure the implementation of the government's policies and programs toward self-sufficienc y in fish and aquatic products.  It will not only address the problem of the increasing domestic demand for fish and aquatic products but also our export on these products, thus boosting the country's dollar revenues.

rows.abstract: "Wife Cruelty Act".  This measure seeks to impose a penalty one degree higher than that provided for by the Revised Penal Code for such offense, especially such as will result in the infliction of physical injuries on the wife, further taking into consideration the aggravating circumstance of the use of superior strength. This bill also provides for the right of the wife to take refuge in government social centers and to eject the habitual wife beater from the conjugal home.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FAIR AND EQUITABLE TERMS FOR THE RELEASE OF MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS' PROFESSIONAL FEE WITHHELD BY HOSPITALS OR MEDICAL CLINICS FOR FAILURE OF THE PATIENT TO PAY HOSPITAL BILLS AND PENALIZING VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to afford protection to medical practitioners by curtailing this unjust practice of some hospitals and medical clinics to withhold the payment of professional fees.  It is the foremost intention of this measure to institute a mechanism that will ensure a fair and equitable terms acceptable to both the hospital and medical practitioners whenever patients make payments of hospital bills.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.
